The company requires all AWS events across every AWS Region in the organization to be recorded and retained in an audit account. It also requires near-real-time notifications for any failed login attempts. A DevOps engineer has created an organization trail in the management account to log events in all Regions. Which solution meets these requirements with the LEAST operational effort?
options: A. Configure the trail to publish logs to a new Amazon S3 bucket in the audit account. In the audit account, create an Amazon EventBridge rule that reacts to failed login events in CloudTrail. Configure the EventBridge rule to notify the SNS topic.

B. Configure the trail to publish logs to a new Amazon S3 bucket in the management account. Configure an Amazon Athena table to read from the new S3 bucket. Create an AWS Lambda function that queries the Athena table for failed login events and publishes the findings to the SNS topic. Create an Amazon EventBridge scheduled rule to invoke the Lambda function every 5 minutes.

C. Configure the trail to publish logs to a new Amazon S3 bucket in the audit account and a new Amazon CloudWatch log group in the management account. Create a CloudWatch Logs metric filter on the log group to create a custom metric for failed logins. Configure a CloudWatch alarm that uses the custom metric and notifies the SNS topic.

D. Configure the trail to publish logs to a new Amazon CloudWatch log group in the audit account. Create an Amazon Kinesis data stream in the audit account. The solution also contains an AWS Lambda function and an Amazon DynamoDB table. The Lambda function retrieves content from an SQS queue event source and writes that content to the DynamoDB table. The solution must maximize Lambda scalability and prevent successfully processed SQS messages from being processed more than once. Which solution meets these requirements?
options: A. Decrease the batch window to 1 second when configuring the Lambda function's event source mapping.
B. Decrease the batch size to 1 when configuring the Lambda function's event source mapping.
C. Include the ReportBatchItemFailures value in the FunctionResponseTypes list in the Lambda function's event source mapping.
D. Set the queue visibility timeout on the Lambda function's event source mapping to account for invocation throttling of the Lambda function.
questions.explanation: Configuring ReportBatchItemFailures in FunctionResponseTypes enables partial batch responses for an SQS event source mapping. Lambda can retry only the failed messages rather than making successfully processed messages in the same batch visible again. With partial batch responses enabled, Lambda does not reduce message polling when invocations fail, preserving processing scalability.

B. Deploy Jenkins to an Amazon ECS cluster and copy build artifacts to an Amazon S3 bucket with default encryption enabled.
C. Leverage AWS CodePipeline with a build action and encrypt the artifacts using AWS Secrets Manager.
D. Use AWS CodeBuild with artifact encryption to replace the Jenkins instance running on EC2 instances.

It currently uses a custom on-premises CI/CD pipeline solution to build and package software. The company wants its software packages and dependent public repositories to be available in AWS CodeArtifact to support creation of application-specific pipelines. Which combination of steps should the company take to update the CI/CD pipeline solution and configure CodeArtifact with the LEAST operational overhead? Choose two
options: A. Update the C1ICD pipeline to create a VM image that contains newly packaged software. Use AWS Import/Export to make the VM image available as an Amazon EC2 AMI. Launch the AMI with an attached IAM instance profile that allows CodeArtifact actions. Use AWS CLI commands to publish the packages to a CodeArtifact repository.

B. Create an AWS Identity and Access Management Roles Anywhere trust anchor. Create an IAM role that allows CodeArtifact actions and that has a trust relationship on the trust anchor. Update the on-premises CI/CD pipeline to assume the new IAM role and to publish the packages to CodeArtifact.

C. Create a new Amazon S3 bucket. Generate a presigned URL that allows the PutObject request. Update the on-premises CI/CD pipeline to use the presigned URL to publish the packages from the on-premises location to the S3 bucket. Create an AWS Lambda function that runs when packages are created in the bucket through a put command. Configure the Lambda function to publish the packages to CodeArtifact.
D. For each public repository, create a CodeArutact repository that is configured with an external connection. Configure the dependent repositories as upstream public repositories.
E. Create a Codeartitact repository that is configured with a set of external connections to the public repositories. Configure the external connections to be downstream of the repository.

Question 131 / Resilient Cloud Solutions A company application uses a fleet of Amazon EC2 On-Demand Instances to analyze and process data. The EC2 instances run in an Auto Scaling group. The Auto Scaling group is a target group for an Application Load Balancer (ALB). The application analyzes critical data that cannot tolerate interruption. It also analyzes noncritical data that can tolerate interruption. The critical-data analysis needs to scale quickly in response to real-time application demand. The noncritical-data analysis consumes memory. A DevOps engineer must implement a solution that decreases scale-out latency for the critical data. The solution must also process the noncritical data. Which combination of steps meets these requirements? Choose two
options: A. For the critical data, modify the existing Auto Scaling group. Create a warm pool instance in the stopped state. Define the warm pool size. Create a new version of the launch template that has detailed monitoring enabled. Use Spot Instances.

B. For the critical data, modify the existing Auto Scaling group. Create a warm pool instance in the stopped state. Define the warm pool size. Create a new version of the launch template that has detailed monitoring enabled. Use On-Demand Instances.

C. For the critical data, modify the existing Auto Scaling group. Create a lifecycle hook to ensure that bootstrap scripts are completed successfully. Ensure that the application on the instances is ready to accept traffic before the instances are registered. Create a new version of the launch template that has detailed monitoring enabled.

D. For the noncritical data, create a second Auto Scaling group that uses a launch template. Configure the launch template to install the unified Amazon CloudWatch agent and to configure the CloudWatch agent with a custom memory utilization metric. Use Spot Instances. Add the new Auto Scaling group as the target group for the ALB. Modify the application to use two target groups for critical data and noncritical data.

E. For the noncritical data, create a second Auto Scaling group. Choose the predefined memory utilization metric type for the target tracking scaling policy. Use Spot Instances. Add the new Auto Scaling group as the target group for the ALB. Modify the application to use two target groups for critical data and noncritical data.
questions.explanation: Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling warm pools keep pre-initialized instances available for faster scale-out. A stopped warm pool with On-Demand Instances is appropriate for critical processing because warm pools do not support Spot Instances in mixed instance groups and the workload cannot tolerate interruption. options: A. In the CloudFormation template, add an AWS Config rule. Add an AWS Systems Manager Resource Data Sync resource to the template to poll for updates to the configuration.

The company uses AWS CodeBuild to build container images and stores the images in Amazon Elastic Container Registry (Amazon ECR). The images are then deployed on Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS). To remain compliant, the company must ensure that images are signed before deployment to Amazon EKS. The signing keys must be rotated periodically and managed automatically. The company must track who generates the signatures. Which solution meets these requirements with the LEAST operational effort?
options: A. Use CodeBuild to retrieve the image that was previously pushed to Amazon ECR. Use AWS Signer to sign the image. Use AWS CloudTrail to track who generates the signatures.
B. Use AWS Lambda to retrieve the image that was previously pushed to Amazon ECR. Use a Lambda function to sign the image. Use Amazon CloudWatch to track who generates the signatures.

Its container-image workflow signs images stored in Amazon ECR, and AWS CloudTrail records AWS Signer API activity to identify the users or accounts that generated signatures. CodeBuild can retrieve the image after it has been pushed to ECR and invoke AWS Signer, satisfying the signing and audit requirements with minimal operational overhead.

questions.questionText: A company runs an Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL global database with two secondary AWS Regions. A DevOps engineer configured the database parameter group to ensure an RPO of 60 seconds. Because of the RPO configuration, write operations on the primary cluster are occasionally blocked. The DevOps engineer must reduce how often write operations are blocked. Which solution will satisfy these requirements?
options: A. Add an additional secondary cluster to the global database.
B. Enable write forwarding for the global database.
C. Remove one of the secondary clusters from the global database.
D. Configure synchronous replication for the global database.
questions.explanation: For an Aurora PostgreSQL global database with rds.global_db_rpo configured, Aurora commits a transaction when at least one secondary cluster has RPO lag below the target and blocks commits only if every secondary cluster exceeds it. Adding a secondary cluster supplies another replication target that can remain within the 60-second window, reducing blocked writes while preserving the RPO requirement.

questions.questionText: A company operates a custom-built application that processes records. All components run on Amazon EC2 instances in an Auto Scaling group. Processing each record consists of multiple sequential, compute-intensive steps. Every step always finishes in 5 minutes or less. A constraint of the current system is that, if any step fails, the application must process the record again from the start. The company wants to update the architecture so the application reprocesses only failed steps. What is the MOST operationally efficient solution that meets these requirements?
options: A. Create a web application to write records to Amazon S3. Use S3 Event Notifications to publish to an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic. Use an EC2 instance to poll Amazon SNS and start processing. Save intermediate results to Amazon S3 to pass on to the next step.

B. Perform the processing steps by using logic in the application. Convert the application code to run in a container. Use AWS Fargate to manage the container instances. Configure the container to invoke itself to pass the state from one step to the next.
C. Create a web application to pass records to an Amazon Kinesis data stream. Decouple the processing by using the Kinesis data stream and AWS Lambda functions.
D. Create a web application to pass records to AWS Step Functions. Decouple the processing into Step Functions tasks and AWS Lambda functions.
questions.explanation: AWS Step Functions provides a stateful workflow for the sequential processing stages, retaining progress between tasks and supporting task-level retry and catch behavior. Each compute stage can run as an AWS Lambda function because its maximum duration is five minutes, which is below Lambda’s 15-minute invocation limit. This eliminates the need to build and operate custom state-passing and failure-recovery logic while allowing only the failed task to be retried.

questions.questionText: A security team configures a workflow that starts an AWS Step Functions workflow when Amazon EventBridge matches particular events. Several AWS services can generate these events. AWS CloudTrail records user activity. The security team finds that some significant events do not start the workflow as anticipated. The CloudTrail logs show no direct errors associated with the missing events. Which combination of steps will identify the root cause of the missing event invocations? Choose three
options: A. Enable EventBridge schema discovery on the event bus to determine whether the event patterns match the expected schema.
B. Configure Amazon CloudWatch to monitor EventBridge metrics and Step Functions metrics. Set up alerts for anomalies in event patterns and workflow invocations.
C. Configure an AWS Lambda logging function to monitor and log events from EventBridge to provide more details about the processed events.
D. Review the Step Functions execution history for patterns of failures or timeouts that could correlate to the missing event invocations.
E. Review metrics for the EventBridge failed invocations to ensure that the IAM execution role that is attached to the rule has sufficient permissions.
questions.explanation: EventBridge only routes events whose structure and values satisfy the rule’s event pattern, so discovering schemas helps validate the pattern against actual events. Amazon CloudWatch provides EventBridge rule metrics for invocation attempts and permanent failures, while Step Functions metrics help reveal downstream workflow behavior. A nonzero EventBridge FailedInvocations metric identifies permanent target-delivery failures; for a Step Functions target, the EventBridge execution role must permit states:StartExecution on the state machine.

Configure the template to have a security group that has an explicit Deny rule on all traffic. Use the CloudFormation template to create an AWS Lambda function that attaches the IAM role to instances. Configure the Lambda function to add a network ACL. Set up an Amazon EventBridge rule to invoke the Lambda function when a specific tag is applied to a compromised EC2 instance.

Configure the template to have a security group that has no inbound rules or outbound rules. Use the CloudFormation template to create an AWS Lambda function that attaches the IAM role to instances. B. Configure a CodePipeline V2 type pipeline that uses SUPERSEDED mode. Add a trigger filter to the pipeline definition that includes all branches. Configure an Amazon EventBridge rule that matches container image pushes to start the existing deployment pipeline.

questions.questionText: An Amazon EC2 instance runs in a VPC and must download an object from a restricted Amazon S3 bucket. When the DevOps engineer attempts to download the object, an AccessDenied error occurs. What could cause this error? Choose two
options: A. The S3 bucket default encryption is enabled.
B. There is an error in the S3 bucket policy.
C. The object has been moved to S3 Glacier.
D. There is an error in the IAM role configuration.
E. S3 Versioning is enabled.
questions.explanation: Amazon S3 returns AccessDenied when authorization is explicitly denied or when no applicable permission allows the action. A bucket policy can deny the request or fail to grant the instance role access, and the EC2 instance’s IAM role can be missing the required s3:GetObject permission or include a deny. Default encryption and versioning do not independently prevent object reads; an object in S3 Glacier must be restored and normally produces an object-state error rather than an authorization denial.

A functional appspec.yml file is in the code repository and contains the following text: A DevOps engineer must ensure that a script downloads and installs a license file on the instances before the replacement instances begin handling request traffic. The DevOps engineer adds a hooks section to the appspec.yml file. Which hook should the DevOps engineer use to run the script that downloads and installs the license file?
options: A. AfterBlockTraffic
B. BeforeBlockTraffic
C. BeforeInstall

questions.explanation: BeforeInstall is a scriptable lifecycle event available for the replacement instances in an EC2/On-Premises blue/green deployment and is intended for preinstallation tasks. DownloadBundle is reserved for the CodeDeploy agent and cannot be used to run scripts.

questions.questionText: A DevOps engineer is developing an application that uses an AWS Lambda function to query an Amazon Aurora MySQL DB cluster. The Lambda function executes read-only queries. Amazon EventBridge events invoke the Lambda function. As an increasing number of events invoke the Lambda function each second, database latency rises and database throughput falls. The DevOps engineer must improve the application's performance. Which combination of steps will satisfy these requirements? Choose three
options: A. Use Amazon RDS Proxy to create a proxy. Connect the proxy to the Aurora cluster reader endpoint. Set a maximum connections percentage on the proxy.
B. Implement database connection pooling inside the Lambda code. Set a maximum number of connections on the database connection pool.
C. Implement the database connection opening outside the Lambda event handler code.
D. Implement the database connection opening and closing inside the Lambda event handler code.
E. Connect to the proxy endpoint from the Lambda function.
questions.explanation: Amazon RDS Proxy provides connection pooling and can limit the database connections it establishes by using a maximum connections percentage, preventing highly concurrent Lambda invocations from exhausting Aurora connections. For a read-only workload, a proxy reader endpoint uses Aurora reader instances and supports read scalability. Lambda should establish the reusable database connection outside the event handler, and its connection string must use the proxy endpoint. Amazon RDS Proxy for Aurora RDS Proxy endpoints for Aurora

questions.questionText: Exams / Amazon / AWS Certified DevOps Engineer - Professional DOP-C02 / A company hosts a static website in an Amazon S3 bucket. Question 157 / Resilient Cloud Solutions A company hosts a static website in an Amazon S3 bucket. Customers access the website at example.com. The company uses an Amazon Route 53 weighted routing policy with a TTL of 1 day. The company has chosen to replace the current static website with a dynamic web application. The dynamic web application uses an Application Load Balancer (ALB) in front of a fleet of Amazon EC2 instances. On the day of the production launch for customers, the company creates an additional Route 53 weighted DNS record entry pointing to the ALB, with a weight of 255 and a TTL of 1 hour. Two days later, a DevOps engineer observes that the former static website is sometimes shown when customers go to example.com. How can the DevOps engineer ensure that the company serves only dynamic content for example.com?
options: A. Delete all objects, including previous versions, from the S3 bucket that contains the static website content.
B. Update the weighted DNS record entry that points to the S3 bucket. Apply a weight of 0. Specify the domain reset option to propagate changes immediately.
C. Configure webpage redirect requests on the S3 bucket with a hostname that redirects to the ALB.
D. Remove the weighted DNS record entry that points to the S3 bucket from the example.com hosted zone. Wait for DNS propagation to become complete.
questions.explanation: Weighted Route 53 records route DNS responses in proportion to their weights; adding an ALB record with weight 255 does not stop the existing S3 weighted record from being returned. Deleting the S3 record removes it from future Route 53 responses. DNS resolvers that previously cached the S3 answer must be allowed to expire that cached entry, so waiting for DNS propagation/cache expiry ensures only the ALB-backed dynamic application is served. questions.questionText: A company mandates an RPO of 2 hours and an RTO of 10 minutes for its data and application at all times. An application uses a MySQL database and Amazon EC2 web servers. The development team requires a failover and disaster-recovery strategy. Which combination of deployment strategies will satisfy these requirements? Choose two
options: A. Create an Amazon Aurora cluster in one Availability Zone across multiple Regions as the data store. Use Aurora’s automatic recovery capabilities in the event of a disaster.
B. Create an Amazon Aurora global database in two Regions as the data store. In the event of a failure, promote the secondary Region as the primary for the application.
C. Create an Amazon Aurora multi-master cluster across multiple Regions as the data store. Use a Network Load Balancer to balance the database traffic in different Regions.

D. Set up the application in two Regions and use Amazon Route 53 failover-based routing that points to the Application Load Balancers in both Regions. Use health checks to determine the availability in a given Region. Use Auto Scaling groups in each Region to adjust capacity based on demand.

questions.explanation: Amazon Aurora Global Database replicates an Aurora MySQL database across Regions, typically with replication latency under a second, and supports cross-Region failover by promoting a secondary cluster. Route 53 failover routing uses health checks to send traffic to the healthy Regional Application Load Balancer, while Auto Scaling groups in each Region provide independent web-tier capacity. questions.questionText: A company uses the AWS Cloud Development Kit (AWS CDK) to develop a microservices-based application. The company must create reusable infrastructure components for three environments: development, staging, and production. The components must include networking resources, database resources, and serverless compute resources. The company must implement a solution that delivers consistent infrastructure across environments while allowing environment-specific customizations. The solution must also minimize code duplication. Which solution meets these requirements with the LEAST development overhead?
options: A. Create custom Level 1 (L1) constructs out of Level 2 (L2) constructs where repeatable patterns exist. Create a single set of deployment stacks that takes the environment name as an argument upon instantiation. Deploy CDK applications for each environment.

B. Create custom Level 1 (L1) constructs out of Level 2 (L2) constructs where repeatable patterns exist. Create separate deployment stacks for each environment. Use the CDK context command to determine which stacks to run when deploying to each environment.

C. Create custom Level 3 (L3) constructs out of Level 2 (L2) constructs where repeatable patterns exist. Create a single set of deployment stacks that takes the environment name as an argument upon instantiation. Deploy CDK applications for each environment.

D. Create custom Level 3 (L3) constructs out of Level 2 (L2) constructs where repeatable patterns exist. Create separate deployment stacks for each environment. Use the CDK context command to determine which stacks to run when deploying to each environment.
questions.explanation: Custom L3 constructs are reusable patterns that compose multiple L2 constructs into higher-level application infrastructure. They encapsulate common networking, database, and serverless resources while exposing properties for environment-specific overrides. Instantiating one shared set of stacks with an environment argument maintains consistent deployments and eliminates the duplicated code required by separate stacks. L1 constructs are low-level CloudFormation resource representations and are not the appropriate abstraction for composing reusable patterns from L2 constructs.

questions.questionText: A company is building an application that will generate log events. The log events include five distinct metrics every one-tenth of a second and create a large volume of data. The company must configure the application to write the logs to Amazon Timestream. The company will run a daily query against the Timestream table. Which combination of steps meets these requirements with the FASTEST query performance? Choose three
options: A. Use batch writes to write multiple log events in a single write operation.
B. Write each log event as a single write operation.
C. Treat each log as a single-measure record.
D. Treat each log as a multi-measure record.
E. Configure the memory store retention period to be longer than the magnetic store retention period.
questions.explanation: Batching multiple records per write operation improves Timestream ingestion performance. Multi-measure records store metrics emitted at the same time in one row, producing more compact storage and lower query latency for multi-metric queries. The memory store is optimized for fast point-in-time queries, while the magnetic store supports long-term storage and fast analytical queries; a daily analytical workload therefore uses a shorter memory-store retention period than magnetic-store retention.

questions.questionText: A company’s application development team uses Linux-based Amazon EC2 instances as bastion hosts. Inbound SSH access to the bastion hosts is limited to specific IP addresses, as specified in the associated security groups. The company’s security team wants to receive a notification if security group rules are changed to permit SSH access from any IP address. What should a DevOps engineer do to satisfy this requirement?
options: A. Create an Amazon EventBridge rule with a source of aws.cloudtrail and the event name AuthorizeSecurityGroupIngress. Define an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic as the target.

B. Enable Amazon GuardDuty and check the findings for security groups in AWS Security Hub. Configure an Amazon EventBridge rule with a custom pattern that matches GuardDuty events with an output of NON_COMPLIANT. Define an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic as the target.

C. Create an AWS Config rule by using the restricted-ssh managed rule to check whether security groups disallow unrestricted incoming SSH traffic. Configure automatic remediation to publish a message to an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic.

D. Enable Amazon Inspector. Include the Common Vulnerabilities and Exposures-1.1 rules package to check the security groups that are associated with the bastion hosts. Configure Amazon Inspector to publish a message to an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic.
questions.explanation: The AWS Config managed rule restricted-ssh evaluates EC2 security groups and is NON_COMPLIANT when incoming SSH is permitted from 0.0.0.0/0 or ::/0. AWS Config can send notifications to an Amazon SNS topic, and an automatic remediation action can use an AWS Systems Manager Automation document to publish the message.

questions.questionText: A company performs vulnerability scans for all Amazon EC2 instances across multiple accounts. The accounts belong to an organization in AWS Organizations. Each account’s VPCs are connected to a shared transit gateway, and the VPCs route internet traffic through a central egress VPC. The company has enabled Amazon Inspector in a delegated administrator account and enabled scanning for every member account. A DevOps engineer finds that some EC2 instances appear in the Amazon Inspector not scanning tab. Which combination of actions should the DevOps engineer take to fix this issue? Choose three
options: A. Verify that AWS Systems Manager Agent is installed and is running on the EC2 instances that Amazon Inspector is not scanning.
B. Associate the target EC2 instances with security groups that allow outbound communication on port 443 to the AWS Systems Manager service endpoint.
C. Grant inspector:StartAssessmentRun permissions to the IAM role that the DevOps engineer is using.
D. Configure EC2 Instance Connect for the EC2 instances that Amazon Inspector is not scanning.
E. Associate the target EC2 instances with instance profiles that grant permissions to communicate with AWS Systems Manager.
questions.explanation: Amazon Inspector uses AWS Systems Manager and SSM Agent for agent-based EC2 vulnerability scanning. An instance must have SSM Agent installed and running, an IAM instance profile that permits Systems Manager to manage it (such as one with the AmazonSSMManagedInstanceCore policy), and outbound HTTPS connectivity to Systems Manager endpoints. Allowing outbound port 443 through the central egress path enables that required SSM communication.

questions.questionText: Exams / Amazon / AWS Certified DevOps Engineer - Professional DOP-C02 / A company uses AWS Directory Service for Microsoft Active Directory as its identity provider (IdP). Question 174 / Configuration Management and IaC A company uses AWS Directory Service for Microsoft Active Directory as its identity provider (IdP). The company requires that all infrastructure be defined and deployed through AWS CloudFormation. A DevOps engineer must create a fleet of Windows-based Amazon EC2 instances to host an application. The DevOps engineer has created a CloudFormation template containing an EC2 launch template, IAM role, EC2 security group, and EC2 Auto Scaling group. The DevOps engineer must implement a solution that joins every EC2 instance to the domain of the AWS Managed Microsoft AD directory. Which solution meets these requirements with the MOST operational efficiency?
options: A. In the CloudFormation template, create an AWS::SSM::Document resource that joins the EC2 instance to the AWS Managed Microsoft AD domain by using the parameters for the existing directory. Update the launch template to include the SSMAssociation property to use the new SSM document. Attach the AmazonSSMManagedInstanceCore and AmazonSSMDirectoryServiceAccess AWS managed policies to the IAM role that the EC2 instances use.

B. In the CloudFormation template, update the launch template to include specific tags that propagate on launch. Create an AWS::SSM::Association resource to associate the AWS-JoinDirectoryServiceDomain Automation runbook with the EC2 instances that have the specified tags. Define the required parameters to join the AWS Managed Microsoft AD directory. Attach the AmazonSSMManagedInstanceCore and AmazonSSMDirectoryServiceAccess AWS managed policies to the IAM role that the EC2 instances use.

C. Store the existing AWS Managed Microsoft AD domain connection details in AWS Secrets Manager. In the CloudFormation template, create an AWS::SSM::Association resource to associate the AWS-CreateManagedWindowsInstanceWithApproval Automation runbook with the EC2 Auto Scaling group. Pass the ARNs for the parameters from Secrets Manager to join the domain. Attach the AmazonSSMDirectoryServiceAccess and SecretsManagerReadWrite AWS managed policies to the IAM role that the EC2 instances use.

D. Store the existing AWS Managed Microsoft AD domain administrator credentials in AWS Secrets Manager. In the CloudFormation template, update the EC2 launch template to include user data. Configure the user data to pull the administrator credentials from Secrets Manager and to join the AWS Managed Microsoft AD domain. Attach the AmazonSSMManagedInstanceCore and SecretsManagerReadWrite AWS managed policies to the IAM role that the EC2 instances use.
questions.explanation: An AWS Systems Manager State Manager association can target managed instances by tags, and dynamic targets are applied as new instances are added to an Auto Scaling group. Associating the AWS-JoinDirectoryServiceDomain document with launch-propagated tags therefore automatically joins each new Windows instance to the existing AWS Managed Microsoft AD domain. The instance role needs AmazonSSMManagedInstanceCore for Systems Manager management and AmazonSSMDirectoryServiceAccess for the SSM agent to access Directory Service and create the domain computer account.

questions.questionText: A company is adopting AWS CodeDeploy to automate application deployments for a Java-Apache Tomcat application that uses an Apache Webserver. The development team began with a proof of concept, created a deployment group for a developer environment, and completed functional tests in the application. Afterward, the team will create further deployment groups for staging and production. The current log level is configured in the Apache settings, but the team wants to modify this configuration dynamically during deployment so it can apply different log-level configurations by deployment group, without maintaining a separate application revision for each group. How can these requirements be fulfilled with the LEAST management overhead and without needing different script versions for each deployment group?
options: A. Tag the Amazon EC2 instances depending on the deployment group. Then place a script into the application revision that calls the metadata service and the EC2 API to identify which deployment group the instance is part of. Use this information to configure the log level settings. Reference the script as part of the AfterInstall lifecycle hook in the appspec.yml file.

B. Create a script that uses the CodeDeploy environment variable DEPLOYMENT_GROUP_ NAME to identify which deployment group the instance is part of. Use this information to configure the log level settings. Reference this script as part of the BeforeInstall lifecycle hook in the appspec.yml file.

C. Create a CodeDeploy custom environment variable for each environment. Then place a script into the application revision that checks this environment variable to identify which deployment group the instance is part of. Use this information to configure the log level settings. Reference this script as part of the ValidateService lifecycle hook in the appspec.yml file.

D. Create a script that uses the CodeDeploy environment variable DEPLOYMENT_GROUP_ID to identify which deployment group the instance is part of to configure the log level settings. Reference this script as part of the Install lifecycle hook in the appspec.yml file.
questions.explanation: AWS CodeDeploy makes the DEPLOYMENT_GROUP_NAME environment variable available to lifecycle hook scripts. A single script can branch on that deployment-group name and update the Apache LogLevel setting for the applicable environment. AWS documents this exact Apache log-level use case and specifies invoking the script in the BeforeInstall lifecycle event, so the same application revision and script can serve development, staging, and production.
learnMore: AppSpec 'hooks' section - AWS CodeDeploy

questions.questionText: A company uses AWS CloudFormation stacks to deploy updates to its application. The stacks contain different resources, including AWS Auto Scaling groups, Amazon EC2 instances, Application Load Balancers (ALBs), and other resources required to launch and maintain independent stacks. Changes to application resources outside CloudFormation stack updates are prohibited. The company recently tried to update the application stack by using the AWS CLI. The stack update failed and produced this error message: “ERROR: both the deployment and the CloudFormation stack rollback failed. The deployment failed because the following resource(s) failed to update: [AutoScalingGroup].” The stack remains in the UPDATE_ROLLBACK_FAILED status. Which solution will resolve this issue?
options: A. Update the subnet mappings that are configured for the ALBs. Run the aws cloudformation update-stack-set AWS CLI command.
B. Update the IAM role by providing the necessary permissions to update the stack. Run the aws cloudformation continue-update-rollback AWS CLI command.
C. Submit a request for a quota increase for the number of EC2 instances for the account. Run the aws cloudformation cancel-update-stack AWS CLI command.
D. Delete the Auto Scaling group resource. Run the aws cloudformation rollback-stack AWS CLI command.
questions.explanation: For an UPDATE_ROLLBACK_FAILED stack caused by insufficient permissions, the CloudFormation service role must be granted the permissions needed to modify the affected resources. The aws cloudformation continue-update-rollback command then resumes the failed rollback and returns the stack to a recoverable state.

questions.questionText: A company uses AWS CodePipeline to deploy an application. Under a new guideline, a member of the company’s security team must approve all application changes before they are deployed to production. The approval must be logged and retained. Which combination of actions meets these requirements? Choose two
options: A. Configure CodePipeline to write actions to Amazon CloudWatch Logs.
B. Configure CodePipeline to write actions to an Amazon S3 bucket at the end of each pipeline stage.
C. Create an AWS CloudTrail trail to deliver logs to Amazon S3.
D. Create a CodePipeline custom action to invoke an AWS Lambda function for approval. Create a policy that gives the security team access to manage CodePipeline custom actions.
E. Create a CodePipeline manual approval action before the deployment step. Create a policy that grants the security team access to approve manual approval stages.
questions.explanation: A CodePipeline manual approval action before the production deployment stops pipeline execution until an IAM-authorized security-team member approves or rejects it. AWS CloudTrail records CodePipeline API calls, including the approval response, and a trail can continuously deliver those audit events to an Amazon S3 bucket for retention.

questions.questionText: A company modified the AWS CloudFormation template for a critical business application. The stack update failed because of an error in the modified template, and AWS CloudFormation automatically started rolling back the stack. Later, a DevOps engineer found that the application remained unavailable and that the stack was in the UPDATE_ROLLBACK_FAILED state. Which combination of actions should the DevOps engineer take to allow the stack rollback to finish successfully? Choose two
options: A. Attach the AWSCloudFormationFullAccess IAM policy to the AWS CloudFormation role.
B. Automatically recover the stack resources by using AWS CloudFormation drift detection.
C. Issue a ContinueUpdateRollback command from the AWS CloudFormation console or the AWS CLI.
D. Manually adjust the resources to match the expectations of the stack.
E. Update the existing AWS CloudFormation stack by using the original template.
questions.explanation: For an UPDATE_ROLLBACK_FAILED stack, CloudFormation could not restore one or more resources to their prior state. The failed resource condition may need to be corrected manually, after which ContinueUpdateRollback resumes the rollback and can return the stack to UPDATE_ROLLBACK_COMPLETE.

questions.questionText: A company develops a stateless application that uses an Application Load Balancer in front of Amazon EC2 instances in an Auto Scaling group. The Auto Scaling group uses a fully prebuilt custom AMI, and the EC2 instances have no custom bootstrapping process. The AMI used by the Auto Scaling group was recently deleted. The Auto Scaling group's scaling activities are failing because the AMI ID no longer exists. Which combination of steps should a DevOps engineer take to meet these requirements? Choose three
options: A. Create a new launch template that uses the new AMI.
B. Update the Auto Scaling group to use the new launch template.
C. Reduce the Auto Scaling group's desired capacity to 0.
D. Increase the Auto Scaling group's desired capacity by 1.
E. Create a new AMI from a running EC2 instance in the Auto Scaling group.
questions.explanation: A running instance launched from the fully prebuilt custom AMI retains the application configuration needed to create a replacement AMI. A launch template must specify an AMI ID, and associating the new launch template with the Auto Scaling group causes subsequent instance launches to use the valid replacement configuration.

Question 180 / Configuration Management and IaC A company that is growing rapidly needs to scale to meet developers’ demand for AWS development environments. Development environments are currently created manually through the AWS Management Console. The networking team manages networking infrastructure with AWS CloudFormation and exports stack output values for the Amazon VPC and every subnet. The development environments follow common standards, including Application Load Balancers, Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling groups, security groups, and Amazon DynamoDB tables. To meet demand, the DevOps engineer wants to automate development-environment creation. Because the infrastructure needed to support the application is expected to expand, the deployed infrastructure must be easy to update. CloudFormation will be used to create a template for the development environments. Which approach will satisfy these requirements and rapidly deliver consistent AWS environments to developers?
options: A. Use Fn::ImportValue intrinsic functions in the Resources section of the template to retrieve Virtual Private Cloud (VPC) and subnet values. Use CloudFormation StackSets for the development environments, using the Count input parameter to indicate the number of environments needed. Use the UpdateStackSet command to update existing development environments.

B. Use nested stacks to define common infrastructure components. To access the exported values, use TemplateURL to reference the networking team’s template. To retrieve Virtual Private Cloud (VPC) and subnet values, use Fn::ImportValue intrinsic functions in the Parameters section of the root template. Use the CreateChangeSet and ExecuteChangeSet commands to update existing development environments.

C. Use nested stacks to define common infrastructure components. Use Fn::ImportValue intrinsic functions with the resources of the nested stack to retrieve Virtual Private Cloud (VPC) and subnet values. Use the CreateChangeSet and ExecuteChangeSet commands to update existing development environments.

D. Use Fn::ImportValue intrinsic functions in the Parameters section of the root template to retrieve Virtual Private Cloud (VPC) and subnet values. Define the development resources in the order they need to be created in the CloudFormation nested stacks. Use the CreateChangeSet. and ExecuteChangeSet commands to update existing development environments.
questions.explanation: Nested stacks provide reusable common infrastructure components for each environment. Fn::ImportValue retrieves the VPC and subnet output values exported by the separate networking stack when used by the relevant nested-stack resources. CloudFormation change sets support reviewing and executing updates across the nested-stack hierarchy with CreateChangeSet and ExecuteChangeSet.

questions.questionText: A company is rolling out a standardized security baseline across its AWS accounts. The accounts belong to an organization in AWS Organizations. The company needs to deploy consistent IAM roles and policies across every existing and future account in the organization. Which solution meets these requirements with the MOST operational efficiency?
options: A. Enable AWS Control Tower in the management account. Configure AWS Control Tower Account Factory customization to deploy the required IAM roles and policies to all accounts.

B. Activate trusted access for AWS CloudFormation StackSets in Organizations. In the management account, create a stack set that has service-managed permissions to deploy the required IAM roles and policies to all accounts. Enable automatic deployment for the stack set.

C. In each member account, create IAM roles that have permissions to create and manage resources. In the management account, create an AWS CloudFormation stack set that has self-managed permissions to deploy the required IAM roles and policies to all accounts. Enable automatic deployment for the stack set.

D. In the management account, create an AWS CodePipeline pipeline. Configure the pipeline to use AWS CloudFormation to automate the deployment of the required IAM roles and policies. Set up cross-account IAM roles to allow CodePipeline to deploy resources in the member accounts.
questions.explanation: AWS CloudFormation StackSets with service-managed permissions use AWS Organizations integration and service-linked roles, so IAM roles do not need to be manually created and maintained in each member account. Enabling automatic deployment deploys the StackSet to accounts added to the targeted organization or organizational units in the future.

questions.questionText: A DevOps engineer operates an AWS CodePipeline pipeline that builds and deploys a web application on AWS. The pipeline contains a source stage, a build stage, and a deploy stage. When correctly deployed, a request to the web application's home-page URL returns an HTTP 200 OK response code. Recently, after CodePipeline deployed the application, the home page returned an HTTP 503 response code. The DevOps engineer must add an automated test to the pipeline. The test must verify that the application returns an HTTP 200 OK response code after deployment, and the pipeline must fail if that response code is not returned during the test. The DevOps engineer has added a CheckURL stage after the deploy stage. What should the DevOps engineer do next to implement the automated test?
options: A. Configure the CheckURL stage to use an Amazon CloudWatch action. Configure the action to use a canary synthetic monitoring check on the application URL and to report a success or failure to CodePipeline.

B. Create an AWS Lambda function to check the response code status of the URL and to report a success or failure to CodePipeline. Configure an action in the CheckURL stage to invoke the Lambda function.
C. Configure the CheckURL stage to use an AWS CodeDeploy action. Configure the action with an input artifact that is the URL of the application and to report a success or failure to CodePipeline.

D. Deploy an Amazon API Gateway HTTP API that checks the response code status of the URL and that reports success or failure to CodePipeline. Configure the CheckURL stage to use the AWS Device Farm test action and to provide the API Gateway HTTP API as an input artifact.
questions.explanation: An AWS Lambda invoke action can run a function after deployment, pass it the application URL through user parameters, make the HTTP request, and test for status code 200. The function reports PutJobSuccessResult when the check passes and PutJobFailureResult when it fails, causing CodePipeline to continue or fail accordingly. AWS provides this exact URL health-check pattern for Lambda actions in CodePipeline.

questions.questionText: A company identifies unusual login attempts across many of its AWS accounts. A DevOps engineer must implement a solution that notifies the company's security team when multiple failed login attempts happen. The DevOps engineer has already created an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic and subscribed the security team to that SNS topic. Which solution will deliver the notification with the LEAST operational effort?
options: A. Configure AWS CloudTrail to send management events to an Amazon CloudWatch Logs log group. Create a CloudWatch Logs metric filter to match failed ConsoleLogin events. Create a CloudWatch alarm that is based on the metric filter. Configure an alarm action to send messages to the SNS topic.

B. Configure AWS CloudTrail to send management events to an Amazon S3 bucket. Create an Amazon Athena query that returns a failure if the query finds failed logins in the logs in the S3 bucket. Create an Amazon EventBridge rule to periodically run the query. Create a second EventBridge rule to detect when the query fails and to send a message to the SNS topic.

C. Configure AWS CloudTrail to send data events to an Amazon CloudWatch Logs log group. Create a CloudWatch logs metric filter to match failed ConsoleLogin events. Create a CloudWatch alarm that is based on the metric filter. Configure an alarm action to send messages to the SNS topic.

D. Configure AWS CloudTrail to send data events to an Amazon S3 bucket. Configure an Amazon S3 event notification for the s3:ObjectCreated event type. Filter the event type by ConsoleLogin failed events. Configure the event notification to forward to the SNS topic.
questions.explanation: AWS CloudTrail records ConsoleLogin activity as a management event. Sending those events to CloudWatch Logs enables a metric filter to match failed console logins, and a CloudWatch alarm can evaluate the count over a specified threshold and publish its alarm notification to Amazon SNS. AWS documents this as the standard alarm pattern for AWS Management Console sign-in failures.

questions.questionText: A company uses AWS Organizations to manage its AWS accounts. The organization root has a child OU named Department. The Department OU has a child OU named Engineering. The default FullAWSAccess policy is attached to the root, the Department OU, and the Engineering OU. The company has many AWS accounts in the Engineering OU. Each account has an administrative IAM role with the AdministratorAccess IAM policy attached. The default FullAWSAccessPolicy is also attached to every account. A DevOps engineer plans to remove the FullAWSAccess policy from the Department OU. The DevOps engineer will replace it with a policy that includes an Allow statement for every Amazon EC2 API operation. What will be the effect of this change on the permissions of the administrative 1AM roles?
options: A. All API actions on all resources will be allowed.
B. All API actions on EC2 resources will be allowed. All other API actions will be denied.
C. All API actions on all resources will be denied.
D. All API actions on EC2 resources will be denied. All other API actions will be allowed.
questions.explanation: SCPs act as a permissions boundary, and a requested action requires an explicit SCP Allow at every level from the organization root through each OU to the account. Replacing FullAWSAccess at the Department OU with an EC2-only Allow limits accounts below that OU to EC2 API operations. AdministratorAccess IAM policies cannot grant permissions that the applicable SCPs do not allow. AWS Organizations SCP evaluation

questions.questionText: An IT team created an AWS CloudFormation template so that others in the company can quickly and consistently deploy and terminate an application. The template provisions an Amazon EC2 instance with a user data script that installs the application, plus an Amazon S3 bucket the application uses to serve static webpages while it runs. All resources must be removed when the CloudFormation stack is deleted. However, CloudFormation reports an error during stack deletion, and the S3 bucket created by the stack remains. How can the team resolve the error in the MOST efficient way, ensuring that all resources are deleted without errors?
options: A. Add a DelelionPolicy attribute to the S3 bucket resource, with the value Delete forcing the bucket to be removed when the stack is deleted.

B. Add a custom resource with an AWS Lambda function with the DependsOn attribute specifying the S3 bucket, and an IAM role. Write the Lambda function to delete all objects from the bucket when RequestType is Delete.
C. Identify the resource that was not deleted. Manually empty the S3 bucket and then delete it.
D. Replace the EC2 and S3 bucket resources with a single AWS OpsWorks Stacks resource. Define a custom recipe for the stack to create and delete the EC2 instance and the S3 bucket.
questions.explanation: Amazon S3 buckets must be empty before CloudFormation can delete them. A Lambda-backed custom resource can handle CloudFormation's Delete request and remove the bucket objects. With a dependency on the bucket, the custom resource is deleted first, so the bucket is empty when CloudFormation deletes it. AWS::S3::Bucket documentation

questions.questionText: A company has one developer who writes code for an automated deployment pipeline. The developer stores the source code for each project in an Amazon S3 bucket. The company plans to add more developers, but is worried about code conflicts and lost work. The company also wants to create a test environment to deploy newer code versions for testing and enable developers to automatically deploy to both environments when code changes in the repository. What is the MOST efficient way to satisfy these requirements?
options: A. Create an AWS CodeCommit repository for each project, use the main branch for production code, and create a testing branch for code deployed to testing. Use feature branches to develop new features and pull requests to merge code to testing and main branches.

B. Create another S3 bucket for each project for testing code, and use an AWS Lambda function to promote code changes between testing and production buckets. Enable versioning on all buckets to prevent code conflicts.

C. Create an AWS CodeCommit repository for each project, and use the main branch for production and test code with different deployment pipelines for each environment. Use feature branches to develop new features.

D. Enable versioning and branching on each S3 bucket, use the main branch for production code, and create a testing branch for code deployed to testing. Have developers use each branch for developing in each environment.
questions.explanation: AWS CodeCommit provides Git-based repositories with branches and pull requests, allowing developers to isolate feature work, review and merge changes, and manage merge conflicts rather than overwriting source files in S3. A testing branch can drive deployment to the test environment, while the main branch represents production-ready code and drives production deployment after approved merges. CodePipeline can automatically detect repository changes and start deployments.

Working with branches in AWS CodeCommit repositories

questions.questionText: A company uses an AWS Organizations organization to manage several AWS accounts that its developers use. The company requires all data to be encrypted in transit. Several Amazon S3 buckets created in developer accounts permit unencrypted connections. A DevOps engineer must enforce encryption in transit for every existing S3 bucket created in accounts in the organization. Which solution meets these requirements?
options: A. Use AWS CloudFormation StackSets to deploy an AWS Network Firewall firewall to each account. Route all outbound requests from the AWS environment through the firewall. Deploy a policy to block access to all outbound requests on port 80.

B. Use AWS CloudFormation StackSets to deploy an AWS Network Firewall firewall to each account. Route all inbound requests to the AWS environment through the firewall. Deploy a policy to block access to all inbound requests on port 80.

C. Turn on AWS Config for the organization. Deploy a conformance pack that uses the s3-bucket-ssl-requests-only managed rule and an AWS Systems Manager Automation runbook. Use a runbook that adds a bucket policy statement to deny access to an S3 bucket when the value of the aws:SecureTransport condition key is false.

D. Turn on AWS Config for the organization. Deploy a conformance pack that uses the s3-bucket-ssl-requests-only managed rule and an AWS Systems Manager Automation runbook. Use a runbook that adds a bucket policy statement to deny access to an S3 bucket when the value of the s3:x-amz-server-side-encryption-aws-kms-key-id condition key is null.
questions.explanation: The AWS Config managed rule s3-bucket-ssl-requests-only evaluates whether S3 bucket policies require SSL/TLS and marks buckets that permit HTTP requests as noncompliant. A bucket-policy statement that explicitly denies requests when aws:SecureTransport is false blocks unencrypted HTTP access, thereby enforcing HTTPS/TLS for data in transit. The s3:x-amz-server-side-encryption-aws-kms-key-id condition instead relates to AWS KMS server-side encryption at rest.

Managing access based on HTTP or HTTPS requests - Amazon S3

questions.questionText: A company uses AWS Organizations and AWS Control Tower to manage all of its AWS accounts. The company has the Enterprise Support plan. A DevOps engineer uses Account Factory for Terraform (AFT) to provision new accounts. When the new accounts are provisioned, the DevOps engineer observes that their support plan is set to the Basic Support plan. The DevOps engineer must implement a solution that provisions the new accounts with the Enterprise Support plan. Which solution meets these requirements?
options: A. Use an AWS Config conformance pack to deploy the account-part-of-organizations AWS Config rule and to automatically remediate any noncompliant accounts.
B. Create an AWS Lambda function to create a ticket for AWS Support to add the account to the Enterprise Support plan. Grant the Lambda function the support:ResolveCase permission.
C. Add an additional value to the control_tower_parameters input to set the AWSEnterpriseSupport parameter as the organization's management account number.

questions.questionText: A company operates a legacy application. A DevOps engineer must automate building the deployable artifact for that legacy application. The solution must save the deployable artifact in an existing Amazon S3 bucket so future deployments can reference it. Which solution meets these requirements in the MOST operationally efficient manner?
options: A. Create a custom Docker image that contains all the dependencies for the legacy application. Store the custom Docker image in a new Amazon Elastic Container Registry (Amazon ECR) repository. Configure a new AWS CodeBuild project to use the custom Docker image to build the deployable artifact and to save the artifact to the S3 bucket.

B. Launch a new Amazon EC2 instance. Install all the dependencies for the legacy application on the EC2 instance. Use the EC2 instance to build the deployable artifact and to save the artifact to the S3 bucket.

C. Create a custom EC2 Image Builder image. Install all the dependencies for the legacy application on the image. Launch a new Amazon EC2 instance from the image. Use the new EC2 instance to build the deployable artifact and to save the artifact to the S3 bucket.

D. Create an Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS) cluster with an AWS Fargate profile that runs in multiple Availability Zones. Create a custom Docker image that contains all the dependencies for the legacy application. Store the custom Docker image in a new Amazon Elastic Container Registry (Amazon ECR) repository. Use the custom Docker image inside the EKS cluster to build the deployable artifact and to save the artifact to the S3 bucket.
questions.explanation: AWS CodeBuild provides managed build environments, supports custom Docker images from Amazon ECR for build dependencies, and can store build output artifacts in an Amazon S3 bucket. This provides repeatable artifact builds without the operational overhead of administering EC2 instances, AMIs, or an Amazon EKS cluster.

questions.questionText: A company has an AWS Organizations organization that includes workload accounts containing enterprise applications. The company centrally manages users from an operations account, and no users can be created in the workload accounts. The company recently added an operations team and needs to give its members administrator access to every workload account. Which combination of actions will provide this access? Choose three
options: A. Create a SysAdmin role in the operations account. Attach the AdministratorAccess policy to the role. Modify the trust relationship to allow the sts:AssumeRole action from the workload accounts.
B. Create a SysAdmin role in each workload account. Attach the AdministratorAccess policy to the role. Modify the trust relationship to allow the sts:AssumeRole action from the operations account.
C. Create an Amazon Cognito identity pool in the operations account. Attach the SysAdmin role as an authenticated role.
D. In the operations account, create an IAM user for each operations team member.

E. In the operations account, create an IAM user group that is named SysAdmins. Add an IAM policy that allows the sts:AssumeRole action for the SysAdmin role in each workload account. Add all operations team members to the group.
questions.explanation: A cross-account IAM role must reside in each target workload account, have AdministratorAccess permissions, and trust principals from the operations account. Operations team members require IAM identities in the operations account, with a group policy granting sts:AssumeRole on each workload account’s SysAdmin role. This supplies temporary administrator credentials without creating users in workload accounts.

questions.questionText: A company uses the AWS Cloud Development Kit (AWS CDK) to define its application. It uses a pipeline consisting of AWS CodePipeline and AWS CodeBuild to deploy the CDK application. The company wants to add unit tests to the pipeline to test various infrastructure components. It must ensure that deployment proceeds only when no unit test fails. Which combination of steps will enforce the testing requirement in the pipeline? Choose two
options: A. Update the CodeBuild build phase commands to run the tests then to deploy the application. Set the OnFailure phase property to ABORT.
B. Update the CodeBuild build phase commands to run the tests then to deploy the application. Add the --rollback true flag to the cdk deploy command.
C. Update the CodeBuild build phase commands to run the tests then to deploy the application. Add the --require-approval any-change flag to the cdk deploy command.
D. Create a test that uses the AWS CDK assertions module. Use the template.hasResourceProperties assertion to test that resources have the expected properties.
E. Create a test that uses the cdk diff command. Configure the test to fail if any resources have changed.
questions.explanation: AWS CDK’s assertions module supports unit testing of synthesized CloudFormation templates, and template.hasResourceProperties verifies that a resource of a specified type has the expected properties. CodeBuild’s on-failure: ABORT setting aborts the build phase when a test command fails, preventing the subsequent cdk deploy command from running.

questions.questionText: Exams / Amazon / AWS Certified DevOps Engineer - Professional DOP-C02 / A company’s development team uses AWS CloudFormation to deploy its application resources. Question 194 / Configuration Management and IaC A company’s development team uses AWS CloudFormation to deploy its application resources. The team must use CloudFormation for every environment change and cannot use the AWS Management Console or AWS CLI to make manual changes directly. The team accesses the environment by using a developer IAM role configured with the AdministratorAccess managed IAM policy. The company created a new CloudFormationDeployment IAM role with the following policy attached: The company must ensure that only CloudFormation can use the new role. The development team must not be able to make manual changes to deployed resources. Which combination of steps meets these requirements? Choose three
options: A. Remove the AdministratorAccess policy. Assign the ReadOnlyAccess managed IAM policy to the developer role. Instruct the developers to use the CloudFormationDeployment role as a CloudFormation service role when the developers deploy new stacks.
B. Update the trust policy of the CloudFormationDeployment role to allow the developer IAM role to assume the CloudFormationDeployment role.

C. Configure the developer IAM role to be able to get and pass the CloudFormationDeployment role if iam:PassedToService equals . Configure the CloudFormationDeployment role to allow all cloudformation actions for all resources.
D. Update the trust policy of the CloudFormationDeployment role to allow the cloudformation.amazonaws.com AWS principal to perform the iam:AssumeRole action.

E. Remove the AdministratorAccess policy. Assign the ReadOnlyAccess managed IAM policy to the developer role. Instruct the developers to assume the CloudFormationDeployment role when the developers deploy new stacks.
questions.explanation: A CloudFormation service role lets CloudFormation perform stack resource operations using the role’s permissions rather than the developer’s permissions. Developers must not retain AdministratorAccess, because it permits direct changes; they should use the deployment role only as the CloudFormation service role. The role trust policy must allow cloudformation.amazonaws.com to perform sts:AssumeRole, preventing developers from assuming it directly. The developer-facing permission to pass the role must be restricted to that role and conditioned on iam:PassedToService being cloudformation.amazonaws.com, so the role can be supplied only to CloudFormation.

questions.questionText: A company has multiple accounts within an AWS Organizations organization. The company's SecOps team must receive an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) notification if any account in the organization disables the Block Public Access feature on an Amazon S3 bucket. A DevOps engineer must implement this change without affecting the operation of any AWS accounts. The implementation must ensure that individual member accounts in the organization cannot disable the notification. Which solution satisfies these requirements?
options: A. Designate an account to be the delegated Amazon GuardDuty administrator account. Turn on GuardDuty for all accounts across the organization. In the GuardDuty administrator account, create an SNS topic. Subscribe the SecOps team's email address to the SNS topic. In the same account, create an Amazon EventBridge rule that uses an event pattern for GuardDuty findings and a target of the SNS topic.

B. Create an AWS CloudFormation template that creates an SNS topic and subscribes the SecOps team’s email address to the SNS topic. In the template, include an Amazon EventBridge rule that uses an event pattern of CloudTrail activity for s3:PutBucketPublicAccessBlock and a target of the SNS topic. Deploy the stack to every account in the organization by using CloudFormation StackSets.

C. Turn on AWS Config across the organization. In the delegated administrator account, create an SNS topic. Subscribe the SecOps team's email address to the SNS topic. Deploy a conformance pack that uses the s3-bucket-level-public-access-prohibited AWS Config managed rule in each account and uses an AWS Systems Manager document to publish an event to the SNS topic to notify the SecOps team.

D. Turn on Amazon Inspector across the organization. In the Amazon Inspector delegated administrator account, create an SNS topic. Subscribe the SecOps team’s email address to the SNS topic. In the same account, create an Amazon EventBridge rule that uses an event pattern for public network exposure of the S3 bucket and publishes an event to the SNS topic to notify the SecOps team.
questions.explanation: AWS Config can evaluate bucket-level Block Public Access settings with the s3-bucket-level-public-access-prohibited managed rule and can use an AWS Systems Manager Automation document as a remediation action to publish to Amazon SNS when a resource is noncompliant. An organization conformance pack centrally deploys the rule and remediation across member accounts; AWS Config organization conformance-pack APIs are available only to the management account or a delegated administrator, preventing member accounts from disabling that centrally managed control.

questions.questionText: A company runs an application in its AWS account. The application uses an Amazon S3 bucket to store objects that include sensitive information. The company must capture object-level S3 API calls, including calls that are rejected because they use invalid credentials. Which solution meets these requirements?
options: A. Create an AWS CloudTrail trail in the account. Enable S3 data events logging. Configure the trail to log to Amazon CloudWatch.
B. Create a new S3 bucket. Configure access logging on the application's S3 bucket. Deliver the access logs to the new S3 bucket.

C. Configure Amazon GuardDuty with S3 protection enabled for the account. Create an Amazon EventBridge rule that matches findings that are associated with the S3 bucket. Configure the rule to use an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) queue as the target.
D. Create an AWS CloudTrail trail and a new S3 bucket in the account. Configure the trail to log to the S3 new bucket.
questions.explanation: Amazon S3 server access logging provides detailed records of requests made to a bucket and delivers them to a destination S3 bucket. AWS CloudTrail data events record object-level S3 operations, but CloudTrail does not deliver logs for requests that fail authentication because the provided credentials are invalid. Therefore, S3 server access logging is required for this condition.

questions.questionText: A DevOps engineer plans to use the AWS Cloud Development Kit (AWS CDK) to manage infrastructure as code (IaC) for a microservices-based application. The engineer must build reusable components for common infrastructure patterns and apply identical cost-allocation tags across the different microservices. Which solution meets these requirements?
options: A. Create a custom CDK construct library that includes common infrastructure patterns. Create a CDK app. Use the TagManager class to add cost allocation tags to the whole app. Use the custom CDK construct library to write a higher-level construct that contains all the microservices. Deploy the microservices as a single CDK stack with environment-specific configurations

B. Create a custom CDK construct library that includes common infrastructure patterns. Create a CDK app. Use the Tags class to add cost allocation tags to the whole app. Use the custom CDK construct library to write higher-level constructs for each microservice. Deploy the microservices as separate CDK stacks with environment-specific configurations.

C. Create AWS Service Catalog products that contain common infrastructure components. Create a CDK app. Use the TagManager class to add cost allocation tags to the whole app. Use the Service Catalog products to write a higher-level construct that contains all the microservices. Deploy the microservices as a single CDK stack with environment-specific configurations.

D. Create AWS Service Catalog products that contain common infrastructure components. Create a CDK app. Use the Tags class to add cost allocation tags to the whole app. Use the Service Catalog products to write higher-level constructs for each microservice. Deploy the microservices as separate CDK stacks with environment-specific configurations.
questions.explanation: AWS CDK constructs are reusable, composable infrastructure components and can be packaged in a custom construct library. Tags.of(app).add() applies a tag throughout the app’s construct scope to taggable child resources, making it suitable for consistent cost-allocation tags. Higher-level constructs can model each microservice, while separate CDK stacks provide independent deployment units for those services.

questions.questionText: A company hosts a web application on Amazon EC2 instances and is deploying the application across multiple AWS Regions. The application includes dynamic content, such as WebSocket-based, real-time product updates. The company uses Amazon Route 53 to manage all DNS records. Which solution provides multi-Region access to the application with the least latency?
options: A. Deploy an Application Load Balancer (ALB) in front of the EC2 instances in each Region. Create a Route 53 A record with a latency-based routing policy. Add IP addresses of the ALBs as the value of the record.

B. Deploy an Application Load Balancer (ALB) in front of the EC2 instances in each Region. Deploy an Amazon CloudFront distribution with an origin group that contains the ALBs as origins. Create a Route 53 alias record that points to the CloudFront distribution's DNS address.

C. Deploy a Network Load Balancer (NLB) in front of the EC2 instances in each Region. Create a Route 53 A record with a multivalue answer routing policy. Add IP addresses of the NLBs as the value of the record.

D. Deploy a Network Load Balancer (NLB) in front of the EC2 instances in each Region. Deploy an AWS Global Accelerator standard accelerator with an endpoint group for each NLB. Create a Route 53 alias record that points to the accelerator's DNS address.
questions.explanation: AWS Global Accelerator provides anycast static IP entry points at AWS edge locations and routes TCP traffic over the AWS global network to the optimal healthy regional endpoint. A standard accelerator supports Network Load Balancers as endpoints, making it suitable for low-latency, dynamic WebSocket traffic across multiple Regions. CloudFront origin groups provide primary/secondary origin failover rather than latency-based distribution among regional origins.

questions.questionText: A software team uses AWS CodePipeline to automate the release pipeline for its Java application. The pipeline has a source stage, followed by a build stage, followed by a deploy stage. Each stage includes one action with a runOrder value of 1. The team wants to incorporate unit testing into the current release pipeline. The solution must deploy only code changes that pass every unit test. Which solution meets these requirements?
options: A. Modify the build stage. Add a test action that has a runOrder value of 1. Use AWS CodeDeploy as the action provider to run unit tests.
B. Modify the build stage. Add a test action that has a runOrder value of 2. Use AWS CodeBuild as the action provider to run unit tests.
C. Modify the deploy stage. Add a test action that has a runOrder value of 1. Use AWS CodeDeploy as the action provider to run unit tests.
D. Modify the deploy stage. Add a test action that has a runOrder value of 2. Use AWS CodeBuild as the action provider to run unit tests.
questions.explanation: AWS CodeBuild supports CodePipeline Test actions and runs the test commands defined for the build project. Adding that test action to the build stage with runOrder 2 causes it to run after the existing build action (runOrder 1); the pipeline cannot advance to the deploy stage unless the test action succeeds. AWS CodeDeploy is a Deploy action provider, not a Test action provider.
